extracted.intended_audience: engineers and proposal managers preparing technical proposals (especially for government/defense contracts)
extracted.subtask_description: A bibliography of sources on preparing, formatting, evaluating, managing, and selling technical proposals, with particular emphasis on government/defense procurement. Useful as a reading list for engineers, proposal managers, and organizations preparing solicited and unsolicited proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow official agency proposal preparation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Guides and general instructions for preparation of proposals (e.g., Air Force Office of Scientific Research 'Guide for preparation of contract proposals', NASA 'General instructions for preparation of proposals').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to agency-specific preparation instructions and submission rules; consult official documents for required sections, formats, and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluator procedures and criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents titled 'Guide for evaluators', 'Technical proposal evaluation procedures', 'Guide to technical evaluation of research and development proposals', and similar describe how proposals will be evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the evaluators' procedures and criteria so proposals can be tailored to scoring and review processes (e.g., appraisal steps, scoring systems, required evidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand how the customer evaluates proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Works such as 'How the customer evaluates your proposal', 'How the military evaluates sales proposals', and 'How NASA judges your unsolicited proposals' emphasize knowing the customer's viewpoint and evaluation priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research customer priorities, weighting of technical vs. cost vs. past performance, and evaluation checklists to align proposal content with what reviewers value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal format and structure (e.g., Five-Parts-Plus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice on specific proposal formats, e.g., 'Your
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use recommended structure (such as 'Five-Parts-Plus') to ensure completeness and reviewer-friendliness, including required sections like introduction, technical approach, management, cost, and qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal style and editorial standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of 'Proposal style guide', 'A style manual for technical writers and editors', and corporate style guides indicates the need for consistent style, tone, and presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply a style guide for consistent language, headings, graphics, numbering, and editorial conventions to improve readability and professional appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist for proposal introductions and executive summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Items such as 'Checklist for proposal introductions' and 'An introduction to proposals' highlight importance of a concise, effective introduction/executive summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure introductions state purpose, key benefits, compliance with RFP, and a clear 'sell' message; use checklists to confirm required elements are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation, brochuremanship, and proposal visuals
rubrics_metrics.description: References on 'brochuremanship', 'presentations', 'staging a presentation', and 'the presentation middleman' stress the role of visuals and packaged marketing in proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance persuasive brochure-style materials with substance; craft visuals and presentations to support the technical narrative without distracting from compliance or detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsolicited proposal preparation and agency-specific unsolicited guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries like 'Guidelines for developing and submitting an unsolicited proposal' for Navy and 'How to write the unsolicited research proposal' indicate special rules and expectations for unsolicited submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow agency unsolicited-proposal procedures closely, emphasize marketability and customer benefit, and include required administrative and technical information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PERT/PERT-COST and scheduling tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple entries discuss 'PERT and PERT-COST in the RFP' and 'PERT-a proposal writing tool'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include credible schedule analyses (e.g., PERT) and link schedule to cost estimates to demonstrate realistic planning and risk management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal management and organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics include 'The proposal preparation cycle', 'Organizing and staffing the proposal team', 'Managing the proposal group', 'Proposal control center', and 'The proposal planning document.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize dedicated teams, define responsibilities, use planning documents and control centers to meet deadlines and maintain consistency across proposal components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selling/marketing the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Works titled 'Selling R and D to the government', 'Preparing proposals that
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame technical content in terms of customer needs and benefits, incorporate marketing concepts (value proposition, marketability), and tailor language to decision-makers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost estimating, pricing, and accounting practices
rubrics_metrics.description: References on 'Accounting for defense contracts', 'Estimating quality control engineering costs', 'What does it cost to make a quotation?', and related financial topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate, defendable cost estimates and pricing models; ensure compliance with accounting practices for government contracts and justify cost assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presenting contractor qualifications and past performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Items like 'Presenting contractor qualification as assets' and 'Contractor past performance records' highlight demonstrating capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document relevant experience, past performance, facilities, and personnel to build credibility; present qualifications as direct assets for executing the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive bidding strategy and bid/no-bid decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries such as 'To bid or not to bid', 'Optimizing R and D bids', 'When/How to propose', and 'Before you bid, know your competition' cover bidding strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use market intelligence, competitor analysis, and profit/effort tradeoffs to choose bidding opportunities wisely and to craft competitive but profitable proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentive contracting, penalty clauses, and 'buy-in' risk
rubrics_metrics.description: References to 'Incentive contracting', 'When are penalty clauses valid?', and 'Performance directive to penalize
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand contract types and risks (incentives, penalties); avoid unsustainable 'buy-in' pricing and ensure terms are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability, integrity and technical accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Works like 'Tips for the reliability engineer — the technical proposal' and 'More integrity needed in reliability proposals' emphasize technical accuracy and integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide honest, verifiable technical claims and reliability analyses; avoid overstated or unsupported technical assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value engineering and total value concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries on 'Total value concepts in contract definition phase' and 'Value engineering in program contracts'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate cost-effectiveness and value-added features; present alternatives or trade-offs that increase program value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measuring proposal effectiveness and marketing ROI
rubrics_metrics.description: Works like 'Measuring the effectiveness of technical proposals and marketing effort' and 'The relation of proposal effort to sales' focus on metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track win rates, cost-to-produce proposals, and marketing ROI to optimize proposal effort and resource allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of critiques and iterative review to improve proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles such as 'Winning R and D proposals through critiques' and 'How the customer evaluates your proposal' imply using critique cycles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct internal and external reviews, incorporate critique feedback early, and use mock evaluations to anticipate reviewer questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal document control and recording
rubrics_metrics.description: References to 'Proposal recording' and 'A central file for company capabilities' stress maintaining records and reference materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep controlled repositories for drafts, boilerplate, past proposals, capability statements, and version history to speed production and ensure consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling mathematical and technical write-ups (clarity/coherence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Works such as 'How to handle math write-ups in proposals' and 'STOP—how to achieve coherence in proposals and reports' address clarity in technical sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear exposition, appropriate visuals, and audio-visual techniques if needed to make complex math comprehensible to reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use and management of boilerplate and standardization
rubrics_metrics.description: Items like 'Let's stop knocking boilerplate (proposals)', 'Standardization speeds proposal output', and 'Shortcuts to proposal preparation'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standardized, pre-vetted boilerplate where appropriate to save time but tailor it to the solicitation to avoid irrelevant or mismatched content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel data and resumes quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles such as 'Building better resumes' and 'Better personnel data for proposals' emphasize quality personnel presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concise, relevant resumes and personnel data that tie experience to contract tasks; emphasize specific qualifications and past project roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team-bidding and teaming procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: References to 'Team-bidding procedures for military development contracts', 'Team bidding', and notes on subcontractor success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define teaming agreements, roles, and responsibilities; clearly present prime/subcontractor relationships and integration plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal introductions and selling points (first page impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple entries about introductions and 'brochuremanship' highlight importance of the opening and front matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft front matter to capture evaluator attention with concise benefits, compliance statements, and clear differentiators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical writing fundamentals for proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: General technical writing resources and papers ('A guide to technical writing', 'The art of technical writing', 'How to prepare effective engineering proposals').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt plain, direct technical prose, logical organization, and reader-centered writing practices to improve comprehension and persuasiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staging and delivering oral/presentation elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Items like 'Staging a presentation' and 'The presentations middleman' address in-person or briefed proposal defense/presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan rehearsed, tightly-focused presentations that mirror proposal themes, highlight benefits, and handle likely questions from evaluators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal planning and scheduling documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Concepts like 'The proposal planning document' and 'An evaluation of the general R and D type proposal using PERT/COST'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit planning documents, schedules, and milestones to show feasibility and program control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with procurement/regulatory trends and contract types
rubrics_metrics.description: References to 'Trends in government contracting', 'DoD shifting to competitive contracts', and 'NASA shifting to incentive contracts' imply adapting to procurement trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stay current with procurement policy changes and tailor proposals to prevailing contract types and evaluation emphases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding proposal anti-patterns and pitfalls
rubrics_metrics.description: Works warning of 'pitfalls in government contracts', 'proposal perfidy', 'dangerous business of defense contracting', and 'brochuremanship — how much is too much?'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid over-selling, unsupported claims, excessive brochuremanship, cost undercutting, and other practices that reduce credibility or increase risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal cost/benefit and profit optimization techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers on 'guide for contractors; stay out of crowds, stop at-cost bidding' and 'optimizing R and D bids' discuss profitability and markup determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use analytic methods to set markups, determine profitable bid strategies, and balance price competitiveness with sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of checklists, seminars and training for proposal improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Seminar/course references and checklists (American Management Association seminars, in-plant proposal-writing workshop, etc.) highlight training and checklists as tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement training programs and standardized checklists to raise team skills and reduce common mistakes in proposal production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of procurement opportunities and agency-specific processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Listings like 'Research and development contract opportunities', 'NASA outlines method of submitting unsolicited proposals', and 'Government contracts handbook' indicate need to document opportunity details and process steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain up-to-date information on solicitations, submission methods, and agency peculiarities to ensure compliance and timely delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal responsiveness and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Guides for 'timely, responsive and successful R and D proposals' and 'producing the overnight proposal' indicate responsiveness as a criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to RFP requirements precisely and on time; adopt processes to rapidly assemble quality responses when needed.
